title: Investigate and remediate cache metadata rollback surge during compaction window
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a 2026-02-27 compaction maintenance window we observed a surge of cache metadata rollbacks that led to tenant-scoped stale index pointers and elevated 5xx rates for prefix-cache reads. Symptoms included a memory transient on compactor nodes, an increase in stale KV read validations, and degraded tail latency for a subset of dedicated tenants. Impact: affected ~6% of active dedicated capacity clusters for ~18 minutes, causing increased downstream retries and two degraded SLAs for customers on older model variants. Root cause hypothesis: a race between concurrent compaction workers and an index-rotation rewrite path caused an out-of-order write sequence. Specifically, compaction could apply a new index file while the metadata journal incorrectly replayed an older rotation marker during an interleaved checkpoint, resulting in a temporary rollback of the namespace metadata (a logical rollback, not filesystem-level). This produced silent divergence where KV lookup paths used stale offsets until a subsequent write reconciled the mapping. Detection: surfaced via a combination of sampled prefix checksum mismatches, elevated validation-failure telemetry, and an oncall report of increased client-side retries. The scrubber detected inconsistent pre/post checksums in ~14 shards. Short-term mitigation already applied: 1) disabled concurrent compaction on compactor type C for the weekend; 2) forced a conservative compaction ordering to ensure older journal segments are sealed before rotation; 3) ran an immediate scrub-and-repair that reconciled ~92% of affected entries and flagged the remainder for manual reconciliation. Long-term impact: risk of repeat under heavy write+compact pressure unless compaction atomicity and journaling ordering are fixed. This ticket coordinates the engineering follow-ups, test coverage, and rollout plan for the fixes and guardrails.
action_items: (Owner: Diego Morales) Implement compaction pre/post checksum journaling: write a pre-compaction signature and verify post-compaction signature before rotating metadata. ETA: 2026-03-18.
(Owner: Linh Tran) Add a compaction coordinator lock for shard-level exclusive ordering across concurrent compactors to prevent interleaved rotation. ETA: 2026-03-22.

(Owner: Priya Nair) Extend scrubber to run in continuous sampling mode with an automated reconcile job for mismatched entries and a quarantine path for entries that exceed reconciliation threshold. ETA: 2026-03-25.
(Owner: Observability) Add telemetry: compaction-duration histograms, pre/post checksum delta gauge, journal-replay-count, and a daily mismatch alert with a 1% sensitivity baseline. ETA: 2026-03-15.
(Owner: QA) Create deterministic integration tests that simulate interleaved compaction + journal replay races and run them in the CI matrix (replicate across 3 shard sizes). ETA: 2026-03-20.

(Owner: SRE) Prepare a canary rollout plan that disables the legacy concurrent compaction flag for 10% of capacity for 48 hours, with automated rollback triggers on mismatch >0.2% or error rate increase. ETA: 2026-03-27.
(Owner: Security) Validate journaling change with security for integrity guarantees and document KMS signing option for checksum certificates. ETA: 2026-04-01.
(Owner: Documentation) Update runbooks and the compaction playbook with new guardrails, rollback steps, and post-incident checklist. ETA: 2026-03-21.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Triage note from oncall: observed spike in prefix-cache validation failures; temporary mitigations applied (conservative compaction ordering).
2026-03-03 — Engineering sync: reproduced failure in local harness by running interleaved compaction and replay; confirmed race window at checkpoint boundary.
2026-03-06 — PR opened: compaction-journal-prepost (draft) for pre/post signatures; requesting design review from storage team.
2026-03-10 — Observability PR merged: checksum-delta metric and daily mismatch alert onboarded to PagerDuty at P4 threshold.
2026-03-12 — SRE performed targeted scrub reconcile on two affected clusters; manual reconciliation completed for remaining 8 flagged shards.
2026-03-14 — Current status: code changes under review; QA harness tests being added; scheduling canary rollout once tests pass.
